verdict.tagline: A punishing survival wilderness where every lesson costs dearly.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep survival crafting challenges
you want a striking hand-drawn art style
you master harsh mechanics through experience
not_for_you_if: you expect clear in-game tutorials and instructions
you dislike relying on external guides and wikis
you cannot tolerate technical startup failures or crashes

distortion_flags.sentence: Player review scores increase steadily as playtime grows past the opening hours.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players face steep learning curves and occasional technical startup hurdles alongside a distinct visual style.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening hours as lacking tutorials or explanations for core systems and goals, requiring external resources to learn how to play.

citations.review_text: This seems to be tailored more for multiplayer, so if you're playing solo, prepare for some weirdness. The game creation process creates a "local server" and is clearly designed to host multiplayer servers. Once you're in, it's painfully boring as single player. There's not even an attempt at bare minimum goal setting or explanation of what anything is. I guess you just wander around and try not to die? Combat is clunky, exploration is boring, and the UI is goofy. Just skip this one unless you have some friends to play with.

This game is not a friendly user experience (UX) as a new player. I work in UX so I'm very cognizant of aspects of an experience like providing information to minimize the amount of time for the learning its  mechanics. Unless I missed something about "help me learn the mechanics" this game is awful as a new player experience. I'm sure there's some external resources, like YouTiube, that can help, but I have too little free time to watch videos to learn to play the game. I'm guessing it gets good once you understand the mechanics, but does not support LEARNING the mechanics... again unless I missed some sort of setting. But why not default such an option and make it an opt out selection. It's a new game, help a person out. I don't want to spent however much time it takes to learn the mechanics. I want to enjoy the mechanics. If i could figure out how to request a refund in team, which I don't know if Steam still offers, I would.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks instructions, tutorials, or clear explanations of how basic mechanics work.

citations.review_text: It does not have any instructions, tutorials, goals... Would probably have been fine playing with someone who already knows the game.

Dogshit game, hates the player. Nothing is explained, have to have a PHD in DST wiki to understand how literally  anything works. Combat is stupid as fuck, every attack is an AOE, doesn't matter which way the enemy is facing you will still get hit. Masochist game, only play if you hate yourself. Don't use the boomerang either its gonna kill you skill issue I guess.

It's a lot like Terraria in many aspects (including the fact that both of them have the Twins (which is also my favourite Terraria boss (#funfact))) but the similarity I want to focus on here is the fact that it is TERRIBLE at teaching new players. Honestly, it's even worse than Terraria in this aspect, since at least Terraria has the Guide and the achievements which help somewhat. But that's just one thing that makes me like this game more. It makes me think all the way back to 2014 when I first played Terraria and I had no fucking clue how to do anything, DST brings back memories from that, however it being even harder to learn this time even kinda fits since now I'm not a drooling child anymore. That's not to mention the difficulty of the game itself. Maybe it's just because I'm really bad, but the game is just extremely hard on its own merit. And I love that! My first time playing this game were with friends who did know what they were doing, and it was just so charming to me, since again it made me think of Terraria where I play with friends who don't know anything and I have to teach them, but in DST I'm the one being taught. Anyway, my point is, this game is an extremely challenging but fun game to play through. Definitely would recommend, especially to Terraria fans.

Awful game, not just the difficulty, which is whatever, but the lack of quality of life things, like why can you not create personal map markers, why do characters like maxwell lose their unique items if they die but yet the guy with the talking axe keeps his. sanity either doesnt matter at all if youre one character or gets you killed by day 3 if youre another. No indication of how basic mechanics work, mobs that follow you forever no matter if youre running on a road (which is faster).

If I was told that game was in Alpha, I'd still think it was released too early. There is no tutorial, commands are super unintuitive, and you can't be safely in base figuring things out looking trough your chests without monsters coming out of nowhere and killing you. There is no tooltip of any kind to know if any food is good or bad, etc.

I've had games where I just didn't understand what people get out of it, but rarely had popular games that I vocally hated. This is game is one of a kind.

I played about 7 hours with my friends and most of us agreed that this game is not fun. Its tedious. While I don't mind grinding and dying, I really dislike that there are absolutely no explanations of how things work. Yes you can eventually figure things out but the frustration is just not worth it.

Gave this game an honest shot, but it just didn't stick after several hours. The artstyle is lovely, but it's overshadowed by a poor new player experience imo. Either include tutorials/hints to teach players how the game works, or make the systems intuitive. I'm afraid Don't Starve does neither of these. Most of my time in this game was spent either frustrated, confused, or a mix of both. 

If you have the patience and/or enjoy working things out with minimal information, you might like this game. But if your patience is limited and you don't like "wiki games", I would avoid Don't Starve.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Experienced survivors embrace the punishing difficulty curve, severe survival elements, and unique presentation.

claims.claim: Reviewers report a steep difficulty curve with harsh punishments like losing progress and permanent world death.

citations.review_text:
I always thought I liked playing hard games, and then I experienced Don't Starve Together...

I do like unique survival games which don't lose their charm after creating your first or second base. However I prefer to come to some likely stable points in the game where you can somehow relax or chill a little. Unfortunately it turns out that Don't Starve is a game where you start without any knowledge and have to learn the hard way since this game is hardcore by default (I know there is a lot to adjust e. g. spawn rates or speed of the day, but I think adjustments in game should only make a game harder or more open for players with barriers). There is a lot that can kill you: the night, the weather, random monster attacks, OP world bosses, hunger and your sanity itself. Anytime you don't know how to handle a situation most of the times you are done except you have a guide by your side. Even though I played about 80h, I didn't enjoy most of the time since the game is so punishing in points of loosing all your progress and save file.

I think that the art style and sound design are very unique in a good way as well as the funny big mob designs. I also appreciate the modding community and updates the game gets after all these years e. g. skill trees for some characters and new characters themselves, but the game should make a hard shift either by adjusting the default difficulty and severity of its punishments, by making player and world progression, as well as world events, about five times faster.

Very very good game, however the extremely sharp difficulty curve and knowledge checks that are heavily punishable such as certain item recipes or game mechanics like seasons often make it a difficult game to pick up if you're new.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks in-game explanations for progression and boss summoning, requiring external guides like YouTube or wikis.

citations.review_text: This games is uncompromising by nature. It will not tell you anything, it will not teach you anything. It will throw you into the constant and wish you farewell. First day you die because of light, next day because of pig, and 5th day because of simple catcoon. Yet you persist, you continue playing and fall in love with this absolutely marvelous game. The content is for thousand of hours. Boss fights are absolutely magnificent, with great design and sound. Mechanics of boss fights are top notch. Give it try, dont give up on first 20 days, because you will give up on day 30 most likely :D but do continue play. Downside of the game, i see in boss summonings. Game does not tell you anything about progression to next fights, you have to try and error, google, youtube in order to find out how to do certain things.

Good Game.

It just keeps updating and mods are plenty. A piece of advice is to have the DST wiki next to you. There are lots of unexplained gimmicks that most players don't know.

As for me, even after 700 hours I still don't know how to summon the final boss. The process is something like; carry some si-fi gizmos around to collect a cave dweller's dust and run errands for a crab lady to fight a glowing spikey ball.

There are lots to do like crashing your ship into a giant tree, setting up automatic farms, starting interspecies wars with spiders, using fire magic, turning into a Were-Canadian, and dying with a full belly. I don't think I've ever starved to death in this game.
